title: Norvo band players: Haymer, Peterson, Purtill
summary: Sauter and Kirchner go through the early sidemen; Herbie Haymer's death.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Do you want to talk about some of the players on the band?
Too bad he died so young. That was really silly. Red tells me he was hit by a car coming out of a recording studio, crossing a street. Some dame was drunk.
Moe Purtill was on that for a while, as you mentioned.
Dave Barbour. And the clarinet player was who? Cook McKirk, Cook Don McKirk.
Later on it was Slats Long.
I'm looking at a book by John Chilton called Who's Who of Jazz. Herbie Haymer was killed in a car crash while driving home--
He was walking across the street, coming out of the recording studio. Red told me that. I always thought it was driving too.
That's interesting. Chilton claims he was killed in a car
crash while driving home from a Frank Sinatra recording session.
The Frank Sinatra recording session is probably correct. You can verify it with Red. Red is the one who informed me he was not driving, he was walking across the street.
I always thought he had gotten loaded and was driving, but the woman who was driving was loaded.
That sounds like some of the stories I heard of people living out in Malibu and getting drunk.
